text:
Maya: Heads-up — after yesterday's AWQ INT8 rollout on prod we see p95 token latencies up ~30% for convo models (v2.4.1 serving runtime + awq weights).
Devon: ugh. is it across all sizes or specific sharded pools?
Maya: Mostly on the dedicated GPU pools (A100 p4d). Small-medium sequence loads (seq<=512) show long-tail. Noticed pack_weights and memcpy spikes in the trace.
Ron: can you paste the flame/profile?
Maya: sure — quick snippet from perf-trace around an inference call:
```
Profile sample (ms):
- preproc/tokenize: 0.8
- kv_cache_fetch: 0.45 / 2.3
- linear_int8_matmul_kernel: 0.9 / 1.6
- pack_weights (AWQ pack/unpack): 1.2 / 3.8
- memcpy H2D (weights/kv): 0.6 / 2.9
- postproc/streaming: 0.5
Total single-token p95: ~12ms (vs 9ms baseline fp16)
```
Devon: pack_weights at p95 3.8ms is suspicious — packing should be offline. are we packing on-demand?
Maya: yes — serving runtime currently does lazy packing on first model load + when group size alignment mismatch occurs. AWQ's group-size=32 default made weight blobs misaligned for our preferred GPU page size, so we trigger a reprog pack on load for some shards.
Sarah: that explains the flash spikes for first few requests + tails when models are swapped between processes.
Ron: also, KV cache behavior with INT8 is tricky: we do small frequent H2D/D2H memcpy for updated KV blocks because the int8-packed layout differs and we currently copy into staging buffers per-token. That adds latency for chat where KV updates per step are many.
Maya: perf-bot ran microbenchmarks earlier today — results (tok/sec / median lat):
```
model: conv-small, seq=256, batch=1
- fp16: 220 tok/s, p50 4.4ms, p95 9.2ms
- awq-int8 (group=32): 185 tok/s, p50 5.8ms, p95 12.0ms
- awq-int8 (group=128): 205 tok/s, p50 4.9ms, p95 10.1ms
- int4 (quant4): 230 tok/s, p50 4.1ms, p95 8.8ms
```
Devon: interesting — increasing group size reduced pack overhead and improved throughput, but int4 still fastest (we already have fused kernels for 4-bit).
Sarah: what about accuracy/regression? AWQ group=128 changes quant noise. Any eval on perplexity or downstream QA?
Maya: ran the eval suite on our standard eval-set: small drop for group=128 vs group=32 in exact-match ~0.6% on rare tokens — within SLA, but need to flag for safety tests.
Ron: actionable items: 1) avoid on-demand packing in hot paths — prepack weights at deploy time (CI step) and store pack alignment metadata; 2) add fused dequant+matmul kernels for AWQ layout to avoid memcpy staging; 3) tweak batching heuristics to reduce small-io KV updates (combine per-client micro-batches).
Devon: +1. For (2) we may be able to re-use existing int8 fused kernels if we align group packing to kernel expected stride (pack-alignment=128). That reduces unpack memcpys.
Maya: we also saw kernel selection fallback in traces: runtime chooses awq-int8 kernel for seq<=512, but for longer sequences or when kv-cache format mismatches, it falls back to fp16 matmul. That path is implemented to be safe but causes perf cliff for mixed workloads.
Sarah: maybe we should refine routing: policy to prefer int8 variant when incoming sequence distribution < 1024 AND model flagged as "awq-friendly". Also add dynamic recompile flag for when pack alignment mismatch is rare.
Ron: calibration note: AWQ/GPTQ calibration affects speed/quality. For AWQ we use per-group scales computed offline with a representative dataset. If calibration uses too short context, scale error grows at long seqs. For safety, keep a secondary calibration for long-context workloads or fall back to per-channel FP16 for top layers.
Maya: we tried bias-correction (GPTQ-style) on final linear layers — it reduced quality gap for group=128 by ~0.3% EM without changing perf. Worth adding as opt-in.
Devon: can we quantify packing overhead vs matmul time? If pack is <10% of total we might accept it, but if it's dominating it's a bug.
Maya: in the bad traces pack/unpack+memcpy accounted for ~35% of tail time for single-token calls. That's unacceptable.
perf-bot: automated regression alert: p95 token latency +28% on conv-small after awq rollout (detected 2024-03-05T12:14:00Z). See run: https://perf.redwood/alerts/2331
Ron: propose quick mitigations: revert awq rollout to group=128 (safe middle), enable prepack CI artifact for upcoming deploys, and flip the packed-fused-kernel feature-flag to on for dedicated pools where tested.
Sarah: test matrix to run before rollout:
- Accuracy eval: EM/ROUGE on eval-suite (baseline fp16)
- Perf: p50/p95 token latency + throughput for seq=[128,512,1024], batch=[1,4,8]
- Memory: peak VRAM and extra staging buffer allocations
- KV tests: steady chat for 500 tokens to exercise KV ops
Devon: I'll pick up the fused-kernel PR. Ron — can you add prepack step to model packaging CI? Maya — can you coordinate canary with ops for dedicated pools?
Maya: yes — I'll open the canary ticket and schedule a 2-hour ramp with traffic shaping.
Ron: I'll add telemetry to surface pack/unpack counts per-model and a histogram for staging buffer sizes. That'll help detect regressions early.
Sarah: also add a QA check: don't allow group-size decreases in model-config without a manual review if it changes packing alignment.
Maya: thanks — moving to action items. If anyone spots odd tail latencies in the next hour ping me. :eyes:
Devon: thanks team.
infra-bot: deploy watcher: canary scheduled for conv-small on pool-dedicated-1 at 2024-03-06T02:00:00Z (UTC).
Maya: noted. I'll post follow-up with canary metrics once complete.
